findings.summary: README says the benchmark's launches are covered, but they run under proton's hook="triton" (line 756), which Compiler.Faithful scope point 3 (part B) excludes
findings.detail: README, Conditions ('The host's use is covered. Every launch the script makes for "mxfp8" meets Inst.ok: the test ..., the benchmark M = N = 8192 with K ... up to 16384') and the bullet for point 9 present the benchmark's launches as covered, and the point-9 bullet names proton's launch hooks only to say that no graph is captured. But the script's __main__ calls proton.start("block_scaled_matmul", hook="triton") (line 756) before every bench_block_scaled call (line 760), and bench_block_scaled makes its timed launches (line 492) between proton.activate() and proton.deactivate() (lines 490-501), after the warm-up launches of line 484. That hook is the launch-enter hook to which Triton hands the decorator's launch_metadata (SEMANTICS.md, Launches, 'launch_metadata=': called 'only when such a hook is installed, which the scope above excludes'). rules/compiler-faithful.md, Scope point 3 ('No hook is installed: knobs.runtime.launch_enter_hook, launch_exit_hook, ...'; '(point 3 bars a hook an API call installs)') and exclusions.md (the 'a hook' row) put such launches outside the rule, and REVIEWER_GUIDE section 1 says that a claim's own launch that visibly breaks a part (B) point is still a finding. So the claim covers the test launch (line 749, made before proton.start) and launches of the benchmark's shapes made with no hook installed, not the benchmark as the script runs it (--bench defaults to True, line 735, so every run of the script profiles). Lean is unaffected (Inst.ok does cover M = N = 8192, K a multiple of 128 up to 2^14). To resolve: say in README (Conditions, the point-9 bullet, and Narrowings and modelling decisions) that the benchmark's launches made after proton.start(..., hook="triton") are outside part (B) point 3 and so not covered, and that the benchmark's sizes are covered only for launches made with no hook installed. SETUP.md, the coordinator's file, says the same as the README and may want the same note.
findings.evidence: source lines 735, 749, 756-760, 484, 490-501; SEMANTICS.md Launches ('launch_metadata='); rules/compiler-faithful.md Scope 3 and 10(c); exclusions.md row 'a hook'

notes: Non-blocking remarks. (1) K <= 2^14 (K_ok) is a narrowing the prover chose so that the tolerance stays meaningful, and the README states it with that reason; the proof needs only an int32 bound on K, and the tolerance tol p (K/128) is explicit for any K. The script's documented use (default K = 512; the docstring's mxfp8 command, K from 8192 to 16384) is covered, so I do not ask for more. (2) The README's sample table matches my recomputation (work/tol_table.py, two seeds of 200 samples each, work/tol_table.out): median tol/|S| 0.053% and 0.057% at K = 512, 0.291% and 0.339% at K = 8192, 0.491% and 0.580% at K = 16384 (README 0.052%, 0.30%, 0.57%); the column 'tol / sum|p| (max)' is a sample maximum, and my two runs gave 1.21e-4 and 1.26e-4 at K = 8192 against the README's 1.0e-4, which is sampling spread, not a stated range. (3) block_scaled_matmul_kernel_cdna4 is launched by the host function block_scaled_matmul_amd (line 700) only on CDNA4 (line 750); neither the claimed launch nor anything on the H200 runs its body, so the unused class is right. (4) The scale path was checked three ways on the CPU (work/scale_layout.py, work/scale_layout.out): the host's reference (unpack_scale, lines 411-417), the kernel's 5-D block, reshape, trans(0, 3, 2, 1, 4) and reshape (lines 223-227, with the zero padding of b's half-outside tile at N/128 odd), and the claim's sIdx give the same byte for every element.
